question: Does CapabilityLoop admit a declared GRPO group whose members have different behavior-policy or verifier provenance, when each member individually passes freshness admission?
scope: VARE local group-contract correctness only; no claim that mixed-policy GRPO is universally invalid.
estimand: For this audit, a declared online GRPO group is intended to represent repeated samples from one requested incumbent policy identity/version and one verifier version. A mixed-provenance group violates that data contract. The numerical illustration compares its score update to the separately specified current-policy on-policy REINFORCE expectation; it is not asserted to be the only valid off-policy GRPO objective.
primary_hypothesis: A group with policy versions [1,0] is admitted and passed to train_candidate when active version is 1 and max_policy_lag is 2, despite the groups representing distinct behavior policies.
primary_outcome: Whether the training hook receives any mixed policy-id/version or verifier-version group.
negative_controls: homogeneous current-policy group [1,1] should be admitted
homogeneous permitted-stale group [0,0] should be admitted under max_policy_lag=2
homogeneous future-policy group [2,2] should be rejected by the existing lag controller
mixed verifier-version group [1,1] should be independently checked

secondary_exact_oracle.policy: Bernoulli target policy pi(a=1)=1/2, reward r(a)=a, group size 2, population-standardized binary group advantages with epsilon treated as zero
secondary_exact_oracle.target_current_policy_expected_update: Under p=1/2 each group gets a nonzero update only when actions differ, an event of probability 1/2; the mean batch score direction is 1/4.
secondary_exact_oracle.mixed_behavior_fixture: One group member sampled from Bernoulli(0.9), the other from Bernoulli(0.1); P(actions differ)=0.82, giving mean target-policy score direction 0.41 if these uncorrected samples are evaluated at pi=1/2.
secondary_exact_oracle.reported_difference: 0.16 absolute, 64% relative to 0.25; this is a specified-estimand contrast, not proof that every mixed-policy GRPO formulation is biased.

falsification: The implementation hypothesis is falsified if the engine or replay rejects all mixed-provenance groups before train_candidate while both homogeneous freshness controls behave as specified.
fix_gate: Patch only if the frozen source-path reproduction confirms admission. The fix must reject a whole group if members disagree on behavior policy identity/version or verifier version; retain homogeneous stale groups within configured lag and current groups.
limitations: No external trainer or language model is run in this v1 protocol.
The RVLGRPOHooks standard rollout path serializes/restores one active policy snapshot; this audit targets the public custom LoopHooks boundary.
Mixed-policy GRPO is an active research direction, so the result cannot be generalized into a claim that heterogeneous behavior groups are inherently invalid.
No capability, task-success, statistical sample-efficiency, or production prevalence claim is in scope.
resources: CPU only; no paid APIs; deterministic fixtures; at most one source-path reproduction and focused regression tests.
stopping_rule: Stop after the baseline source-path reproduction, the minimal fix if confirmed, and focused regression tests. Do not extend to broad benchmark or model training.
